en.title: Unordered Node Pairs on a Tree Rearrangeable into a Palindrome
en.description: In an undirected tree, edge weights 1..26 correspond to a..z. For two distinct nodes, take all edge letters on the unique path between them; if these letters can be rearranged in any order into a palindrome, the unordered node pair is a nice pair. Find the number of nice pairs. The path string does not need to be a palindrome already; a node is not paired with itself, and the two directions are not counted twice.
en.input: The first line contains n m, followed by m lines of u v w. Full original constraints: 1≤n≤100000, m=n−1, 1≤u,v≤n, 1≤w≤26; the input is guaranteed to form a tree whose diameter, in edges, is strictly less than 1000. Nodes are 1-based.
en.output: Output the number of unordered nice pairs of distinct nodes, using a 64-bit integer; for a single-node tree, output 0.
en.explanation: The three public examples keep, respectively, the 9 of 019, the 7 of 021/022, and the 10 of 023/024. In 019, BAA can be rearranged into ABA, so it counts too; a five-node all-A tree has C(5,2)=10 pairs. 018 has a different topology with a true answer of 8; this site covers it separately and does not mix it up with the 9 of 019.
hints: Rearranging into a palindrome only requires checking frequency parities.
XORing the parity masks of the two root paths gives the mask of the path between the nodes.
Query the nodes seen so far before inserting the current node, which excludes self-pairs and double counting.
